title: What the familiar brought
steps: You have a handful of pieces of black thread in your hand. Above, a bolt is heard, and steps on the back stair. Rinlo comes out of the arch at the end of the corridor, very pale.

Flying terrifies me. Before every lesson I spend days without sleeping. The voice knew it. It spoke to me from a wall, promised me the lessons would stop and nobody would get hurt, and showed me the knot. I didn't know what the knot did! And today it wanted me to tie it to you.
"I don't like brooms either," says {mate}. Rinlo nearly laughs.

The four of you go up to the tower. Orla is alone with the book. You lay the threads on the lectern. "They're threads for tampering with brooms," says {friend}. You tell her everything, even that you were out of bed that night.
They are far more than that. They are the leavings of the soul of a wizard who was killed with a black spell. They are evil itself, made a thing by that death.
They cause harm that cannot be told. They draw death and pain. They destroy friendship, and the soul.
"I've had them in a box for months," says {friend}, with hardly any voice.
Loose, they sleep. It is the knot that wakes them. You did well to untie them, and better to bring them to me.

Orla covers them with a cloth and locks them away: "That knot has not been taught in Arvelia for many years. I believe you." And to Rinlo: "You told it no. That was the hardest thing, and you did it on your own."
Sit down. There is something you must know, and you more than anyone, {wizard}.
